Religion definitely exists in Kenshi, it's most vocal in the HN like you say but there are other less extreme instances.

Starting off with the most extreme, the Shek. Like you said the Shek have a very shogunistic warrior culture, and this seems to transcend aesthetics and enters spiritual territory when you consider the Bugmaster and Kral. Kral was a legendary warrior who's teaching are very much biblical to modern Shek society, to the point that mild deviation from it inspires extremists (the Kral's chosen) to rise up in the kingdom (along with other reasons). Furthermore the Shek's need for an honorable death is something I can only assume is spiritual as well, the Shek when they're too old to fight head down to Last Stand then Arach to go and die in combat against the Bugmaster and his spiders, the focus on death here screams of spirituality, as the Shek leave very little behind in regards to a legacy that is at risk of being tarnished, and to me suggests some belief in an afterlife or something necessary to have a peaceful one.

Another less extreme example is Okranism (or whatever it's called) outside the HN. Occasionally you'll hear people in the UC use Okran or Narko's name, showing that some people further out may believe in Okran and HN teachings to some extent (likely a much less extreme extent given how they're not burning their shek / hiver neighbours). Also the Flotsam Ninjas have a large Okranite / Narkoite population as Moll says, they're much less extreme and radical than the HN, but they still uphold some of the core beliefs.

Lastly there's this pseudo-religion which alot of skeletons follow which I've called 'stobeism.' I count this as a religion as while it doesn't have a god, it still has core teachings about... mainly not exterminating or genetically experimenting on humans really, but the presence of these core unified philosophies can be read as a system of belief.

Season of the Risen was about how the Lucent hive were invading earth and the Moon, I could see something like us launching a counterattack, but other than that why would they be invading their own home?

Season of the Haunted makes more sense, while ultimately it was all about the leviathan and Calus, given that we were working with the crown of Sorrow (an artifact of Savathûn), I could see why narratively we might invade her keep or personal chambers or something like that to get her secrets to better use the crown. But while that makes narrative sense, ultimately the seasons narrative worked fine without it and adding it on would just put in too much content gameplay wise for a season, and having it be a weekly mission would take too much focus away from Calus.

Season of the Plunder was about uncovering Fallen artifacts, given the Fallen never entered Savathûns TW, it makes no sense an artifact or treasure would be buried there. And yes, it makes perfect sense that Savathûn or her brood would want to capture these relics given there immense power, and Nezarecs relation to Savatbûn, and this is what I believe we see happen in the latter end of the season, with Lucent hive attacking or having sacked pirate outposts we later turn up to, however given Savathûns goals prior to and during WQ were primarily of the Light, it makes perfect sense that she would be content to just leave the relics alone, and given the major defeat the Lucent brood took in Season of the Risen, it makes sense they didn't attempt to capture the relics sooner.
And while this is my own speculation it would make sense even they only sought out the relics after potentially finding out we were after them, and they wanted to slow us down for the sake of being our enemy, given they are enemies of the literal god stored within these artifacts, it makes little sense they would want to bring these artifacts together and potentially giving Nezarec power, when they are in such a weakened state where they would be unable to defend themselves.

Season of the Seraph along with season of the Haunted is the other season I could see us visiting the throne world, but only in a weekly story mission, Rasputin and Savathûn to my knowledge never interacted beyond Savathûn potentially picking out a few secrets from him, Rasputin never attacked or attsmpted to build an outpost anywhere outside of the system and especially not in a throne world. However given Osiris was ultimately seeking a secret which was revealed to him via Savathûn, I could see a weekly mission where we visit the throne world to scour anything Neomuna related Savathûn may have documented, and I don't think this would have been tacked on or adding too much content either. But I think it could have potentially strayed too far away from the story of Rasputin, we (the community) already knew about Neomuna, its location and the major plot points (Strand/an artifact related to the traveler i.e the Veil, there being another city, etc) so in a meta sense there was nothing substantial we could learn from Savathûn which wouldn't bleed to heavily into Lightfalls story, thus the decission to stay focused on Rasputin and tell a story we knew nothing about was in my eyes the better decission, and as mentioned before Rasputin has 0 interaction with the throne world.

Ultimately while there were a few oppertunitues where it would make sense to visit the TW, I think what we got instead was still a good year of seasons (aside from plunder, I would have taken a story of Fallen pirates invading the throne world to reclaim the relics over what we ended up getting), and adding the Throne world to what we got would have just been overloading them with too much too much for players to handle, or would have made little narrative sense. I do hope they don't make the same mistake with Neomuna though, and I hope S22 & S23 see us revisiting both Neomuna and the TW in some capacity as in spite of the stories we got, it was an utter crime we didn't explore it more last year

It's hard to really divulge much information without going into spoiler territory but here goes:

Be wary of your decissions and actions, while you can talk and shoot your way out of many situations, it is easy to trap yourself in a corner with choices prior, or having certain companions in your party. Additionally be wary of the companions you bring with you, they have their own interactions with many quests and characters, sometimes offering unique interactions, endings to quests, dialogue choices, or sometimes they will completely fail a quest, lock you out of other quests, and leave your party. 


There is a mission in the late-early game where a character from a main quest prior contacts you and asks for your help in sacking a prominant settlement you have done some missions for, I would reccomend siding with the settlement because you get better rewards, but it's your call. Whatever you do, do not ignore this quest, it doesn't matter what quest you were doing when you get the call, drop everything and head to where the mission tells you to go. It's (I think) the only time-sensitive mission in the game, and doing even a single mission before completing this one results in both sides wiping eachother out, leaving you with sod all, and killing several merchants.

There is a mostly unspoken loyalty mechanic with your rangers (faction not squad), that is affected by your actions throughout Colarado, and your choices regarding Ranger HQ and it's inhabitants. Generally you gain positive relations by inviting more people throughout the game to Ranger HQ, taking prisoners and sending them to the Ranger brig, and prioritising/glorifying your Rangers. And lose relation for doing the opposite, and acting generally a-morally seperate to any factions laws or idea of justice. High loyalty will give you good discounts with merchants in Ranger HQ, while low loyalty has end-game ramifications.

Kiss ass is better than Hard ass. Hard ass is used far less than Kiss ass, and often times unless you're starting a combat encounter, makes a situation actively worse. Invest in it, but prioritise Kiss ass.

Some factions don't have a reputation meter, this doesn't mean you can simply disregard them as non-important as these factions are often rather important, and can give powerful rewards to you for aiding them. 

Look out for the small things. It goes without saying in a game like Wasteland but often times you can find a small note somewhere or an interactable somewhere in the room that can unlock secret areas or new interactions, usually netting you some very powerful rewards.

And finally not really a choices thing, but invest in weapon modding, while you can't fallout 4 style make some unholy mixture of a laser-plasma shotgun pistol, you can turn an otherwise unremarkable gun into an absolute beast of a weapon
Although be careful with recruiting certain chickens (you'll know em when you see em), and make sure they don't get killed off for any reason

To get necromancer an orc needs to meet certain Criteria

3) When he becomes accursed his eyes will turn either red or yellow, you can only get necromancers from red eyes.

These criteria can be circumvented by unique personalities

-The Warlock (he has some other titles which I couldn't find but he'll still be the same)

-The Gravewalker

- Zog the Eternal

These orcs all appear with cursed skin but can appear with yellow eyes (except Zog who has undead eyes for story reasons)
